commitResults.messageBody:
The project lacks persistent instructions for Java style, Git history, and UI regression testing.

Add the project-specific skills and package the Java sources so future refactors follow a consistent baseline.

Gary mixes command handling with console input and output, which makes the application flow difficult to follow.

Move all terminal interactions into Ui so Gary can focus on coordinating chatbot behavior.

Gary interprets command syntax, task details, dates, and task numbers in addition to coordinating application behavior.

Move input interpretation into Parser so command handling has one focused source of validation rules.

Gary owns the task collection and performs every mutation, which exposes collection details throughout the command loop.

Move task storage and mutations into TaskList and keep Gary focused on coordinating the parser, UI, storage, and task list.

All classes sit in one package despite having distinct responsibilities.

Move each responsibility into a focused subpackage.

Keep src/main/java as the source root.

The project needs a reproducible build and application launcher.

Merge the provided Gradle wrapper and build configuration into master.

The provided build targets the template's Duke class and artifact name.

Point the application plugin at Gary.

Name the packaged artifact gary.jar to match the chatbot.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit coverage for core behavior
commitResults.messageBody:
Core behavior has no automated regression coverage.

Add focused tests for commands, task state, and storage.

Document the 50% high-value coverage target for future changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Javadoc for task manager API
commitResults.messageBody:
The public API lacks documentation of its purpose and behavior.

Document all production classes and their exposed operations so that callers
can understand their contracts without reading implementation details.

The production and test classes use the default package and contain layout
that does not satisfy the project's required Java standard.

Organize related classes into lower-case packages, align the tests with their
production packages, and normalize wrapping and switch indentation.

Java changes need a durable project rule so future contributions continue
to follow the course standard.

Add a project skill containing the required checks and make its use mandatory
in the repository agent guidance.

Commit quality depends on applying the course conventions consistently
after this increment.

Add a focused Git-standard skill and require agents to load it before creating
branches, commits, merges, or tags.

Visual reviews require the diff generator to be available to every clone of
the project rather than only in this working copy.

Track the existing project skill and its self-contained HTML generator.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find command: Add task description search
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot retrieve tasks by description without reading the entire list.

Add a case-insensitive find command that retains original task numbers.
Reject empty keywords, and cover command recognition and keyword matching in
JUnit.

Bring the completed API documentation into the integration branch while
preserving the parallel feature branch in history.

Integrate the package and coding-standard work together with the reusable
project skills that keep future Java and Git changes compliant.

Configure Gradle to check production and test sources against the SE-EDU Java coding standard.

Import the shared rules and align existing tests with their import ordering and line-wrapping requirements.

Add an FXML-based conversation window with reusable dialog controls.

Use a separate launcher so packaged JavaFX execution works reliably.

Share command processing between the GUI and terminal interface.

Keep task behavior and persistence consistent across both entry points.

Centralize multi-line response construction in one varargs helper.

Keep command output consistent while removing repeated separator handling.

Several components depend on non-null commands, valid task positions, and
complete task data passed between trusted layers. Violations can fail later
and obscure the source of programming errors.

Add Java assertions at parser, storage, task, and command-processing
boundaries. These assertions document the contracts and fail close to the
defect when assertions are enabled, while preserving normal validation for
recoverable user input.
Add assertions for internal invariants

Command dispatch uses a long conditional chain even though commands use
finite enum values. The fallback also hides whether every value has been
considered.

Use a switch expression to keep commands beside their actions.
This lets the compiler detect missing cases as the command set changes.

Deadline and event parsing repeat the same conversion and exception
translation. Short local names also blur the distinction between raw
input and parsed dates.

Extract one date conversion helper and rename intermediate values.
This removes duplication and makes each parsing step read at one level
of abstraction.

Task record parsing mixes validation, date conversion, and object
construction in nested expressions. Numeric field positions also hide
the record layout.

Extract named constants and one parser for each task type. This keeps
the happy path prominent and gives each method one abstraction level.

commitResults.messageTitle: Task classes: Make identity data immutable
commitResults.messageBody:
Task descriptions and dates never change after construction, but their
fields remain mutable. This suggests unsupported state changes and makes
the object invariants less explicit.

Declare those fields final. Completion status remains mutable because
marking and unmarking are intentional task operations.
Improve code readability and maintainability

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Use streams for record conversion
commitResults.messageBody:
Loading and saving tasks use manual loops for collection conversion.
The loop bodies only transform elements and filter invalid records.

Use stream pipelines to express those operations directly. Preserve the
existing ArrayList return contract while making each conversion stage
explicit.
Use streams for task record conversion

Gary manages tasks but cannot store information about people. Users need
a separate contact workflow that does not interfere with task commands.

Add commands to create, list, search, and delete contacts with names,
phone numbers, and email addresses. Persist contacts in a separate data
file to keep task storage compatible. Reject incomplete input with clear
errors.

Cover parsing, storage, lifecycle, failures, and reload behavior with
JUnit and terminal UI tests.
Add persistent contact management
